1.explanation: • discover_preview_images in discover_preview_images.lua is the filter that picks off page images for the gallery. If it misclassifies or drops relative URLs after punctuation, that will break the preview. • templateMarkdownHandler in website-listing-template.ts is where the listing’s HTML (including ) is generated for the grid. It likely needs to handle or normalize non-http paths differently. • resolveItemForTemplate is responsible for shaping item data (including image URLs) before templating; if it doesn’t properly escape or preserve commas/paths, the grid src attribute can become invalid. • joinUrl in core/url.ts is used to build absolute URLs from a base + path; if it’s invoked on a relative path with punctuation, it may yield a malformed host:// path. • ensureProtocolAndTrailingSlash in core/url.ts unconditionally prefixes non-http URLs with “https://” and adds a slash, which turns a relative asset path like “diet-assets/clabberedMilk.jpg” into “https://diet-assets/clabberedMilk.jpg/”, causing a 404 in the grid. All of these functions participate in discovering, normalizing, and emitting the image src. Fixing how they treat non-http, punctuation-heavy, or relative paths will restore the preview in the grid view.
1.bug_scenario: The user’s QMD page includes both a web‐hosted image URL (with punctuation) and a local relative image path “diet-assets/clabberedMilk.jpg”. When rendered inline in the post, both images display correctly. However, in the site’s gallery/grid view (generated by the website listing pipeline), the preview pane shows a broken image icon for the non-standard URL/path. The grid generator appears to be mangling or rejecting relative URLs that contain commas or other punctuation, or else unconditionally adding a protocol slash to them, which leads to an invalid src in the preview. The result is that only standard https:// URLs work in the grid, while relative paths and unusual filenames fail.

2.explanation: The discover_preview_images.lua filter only processes a single Image element (due to the `set` flag), preventing multiple previews from being discovered in the grid. The URL utilities in url.ts (isHttpUrl, joinUrl, ensureProtocolAndTrailingSlash) govern how local versus HTTP URLs are recognized and constructed—non-standard paths with punctuation may slip through or be misassembled, causing broken previews. Finally, templateMarkdownHandler in website-listing-template.ts is responsible for collecting and rendering those discovered image URLs into the listing grid; if URLs aren’t recognized or images aren’t discovered, the grid shows no preview. Fixing these functions will allow all images (including those with punctuation in their paths) to be discovered and correctly displayed in the grid preview.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering a blog post with images both from the web and a local file path containing punctuation (e.g. “diet-assets/clabberedMilk.jpg”), the inline images show up correctly in the post but the gallery or grid preview fails to display those images (they appear broken or missing).
